title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous pages Grothendieck proves that the boundary at infinity M̂^∞ = M̂_G \ M_G of the Deligne–Mumford compactification is connected. He reduces to M̂_{g,I} with N = dim = 3(g-1)+ν ≥ 3, since the case N = 2 was already treated. The boundary is a union of irreducible divisors, and each of these is connected. So it suffices to show that any two boundary divisors can be joined by a chain of boundary divisors in which consecutive ones meet. Previous page (90): the divisors are indexed by stable graphs with one edge:
- a) one vertex of genus g-1 with a loop (Δ_irr), which exists iff g ≥ 1;
- b) two vertices (g',I'), (g'',I'') with g'+g'' = g and I' ⨿ I'' = I, with the stability condition card I' ≥ 2 if g' = 0.

This page:
- (91) α) is the codimension-2 stratum given by a vertex of genus g1 with a loop, joined by an edge to a vertex of genus g2, with g1+g2 = g-1. It lies in the closure of a). For example one can take g2 = 1, g1 = g-2 (g ≥ 2) with an arbitrary partition (I1, I2) of I.
- (92) b') is the stratum obtained from b) by putting a loop on the vertex g', which then gets genus g'-1. It lies in both a) and b), so it is a common specialization.

If g ≥ 1, then g'+g'' = g forces one side, say g', to be ≥ 1 (WLOG g' ≥ g''). So every divisor of type b) meets Δ_irr, and all boundary divisors are linked through Δ_irr. This proves the claim for g ≠ 0.

For g = 0 (so ν ≥ 6, given N ≥ 3) there are only type-b) divisors D_{I'|I''}. Each contains a 0-dimensional stratum b″) (93): a 'caterpillar' chain of P^1's. The end vertices carry 2 marked points and the interior vertices carry 1. The left part has k edges, k+1 vertices and 2+k = card I' points; the right part has ℓ edges and 2+ℓ = card I'' points. The middle edge is the node of D_{I'|I''}. Such maximal degenerations correspond to total orders on I modulo swapping the first two and the last two elements.

Next page: two adjacent orders (differing by a transposition of consecutive c_i, c_{i+1}) give 0-strata lying on a common boundary divisor, namely the one obtained by contracting the edge c_i–c_{i+1}. Since transpositions generate S_ν, all g = 0 boundary divisors are chained.

Purpose: this is part of the 'structure at infinity' programme, i.e. understanding the neighbourhood at infinity of M_{g,ν}, its connectedness and fundamental group at infinity, relevant to the Teichmüller tower and tangential base points.
errors: 'donc card I ≥ 6' in the g = 0 case: from N = ν-3 alone one only gets ν ≥ 5. The ≥ 6 is correct because the case N = 2 was handled separately ('dans OPS N≥3' on the previous page). This is consistent, not an error.
The aside 'on peut prendre g2=1, g1=g-2 pourvu que g≥2' is not needed for the argument: b') already gives the common specialization of a) and any b) with g' ≥ 1. It is harmless.
In b″) the weight bookkeeping (end vertex weight 2, others weight 1, total 2+k) is correct. It implicitly requires card I', card I'' ≥ 2, which genus-0 stability guarantees.

ideas.what: Boundary divisors of M̄_{g,n} indexed by one-edge stable graphs (Δ_irr and Δ_{h,S}), with codimension-2 strata as common specializations
ideas.modern_name: Stratification of M̄_{g,n} by stable dual graphs; boundary divisors Δ_irr, Δ_{h,S}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford (1969), Knudsen (1983); systematised by Arbarello–Cornalba and others
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the stratification at infinity and the Teichmüller tower qualitatively

ideas.what: Connectedness of the boundary of M̄_{g,n} (dim ≥ 2) via chains of intersecting divisors; every Δ_{h,S} meets Δ_irr when g ≥ 1
ideas.modern_name: Connectedness of ∂M̄_{g,n} / connectedness of the boundary dual complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; follows from Harer's connectivity of the curve complex; the dual complex is studied by Chan–Galatius–Payne

ideas.what: Genus 0: maximal degenerations as caterpillar trees ↔ total orders on I modulo swapping the first two and last two points; adjacency via transpositions
ideas.modern_name: 0-dimensional (caterpillar) boundary strata of M̄_{0,n}; connectivity via adjacent transpositions (cf. Kapranov, associahedra and permutohedra combinatorics)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean but elementary combinatorial proof of a well-known fact (connectedness of the DM boundary). The caterpillar description of the 0-strata of M̄_{0,n} is standard. It is historically nice as an early, independent treatment, but contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The insertion above 'une spécialisation' reads '(b′) = a′))' rather than 'b′) → a′)'. It indicates that this b′) is the same as the α)-type stratum.
'i.e. que g'·g''' should likely read 'i.e. que g' ≥ g''' (the WLOG normalisation).
Margin under (91): 'pourvu que g≥2' attaches to 'on peut prendre g2=1, g1=g−2'; also '(I1,I2) partition quelc. de I'.
In (93) the right-hand labels are (b_ℓ)(b_{ℓ−1})…(b_2)(b_1)(b_0) with weights 1,…,1,2. The note under the left brace reads 'y a un poids marqué total 2+k = card I′'.
